title: Nashville Hot Chicken Nuggets
summary: The same juicy ground chicken and pork nuggets, breaded and fried, then dunked in a cayenne, smoked paprika and brown sugar spice oil made with the hot frying oil.
notes: Video: 'Easy Chicken Nuggets at Home' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). The video holds two versions (house rule 6), both in files pointing to the same transcript: plain nuggets and Nashville hot nuggets dunked in spice oil. No written recipe was used: the joshuaweissman.com page for this video could not be retrieved (www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/easy-chicken-nuggets-at-home returned an error), so servings and times rest on the video alone. Servings: 4, our estimate. The video gives no yield; the mixture is about 760 g raw, which at the 1 1/2-2 oz scoop he uses makes roughly 13-18 nuggets. Prep and cook times are left empty: the video gives only part times (3-4 minutes per frying batch); the farce rests in the fridge at least 3 hours, ideally overnight, which would not go in prep_minutes anyway (house rule 13). Our estimates: 1 1/2 Tbsp ice water ('a tablespoon or two'); large eggs (size not said). House rules applied: flour and panko count at 25% and the egg wash at 50%; the deep-frying oil is excluded and 89 g of absorbed oil is counted (arithmetic on that line). Both sauces (chili crisp garlic mayo, and honey mustard, which uses about 1/3 cup of the mayo) are served on the side and not counted; the mayo alone is about 1 cup of oil, about 1,900 kcal for the batch if all of it is eaten. Not counted: the splash of water in the egg wash and salt to taste in the sauces. Panko uses USDA plain dry breadcrumbs, which are denser per cup than panko, so a cup-based weight may overstate the coating. Chili crisp and Dijon are only in the side sauce and need proxies (see new_h2.csv). Version 2: Nashville hot. All nuggets are assumed dunked ('repeat with as many nuggets as you like'). The spice oil is a dunking oil made in a bigger batch than stays on the nuggets and no share is stated, so every spice-oil line counts at 25% (house rule 10; full batch kept in each line's text). '2 tbsps of garlic' in the spice list is read as garlic powder.

steps.text: Put the ground chicken and the fatty ground pork in a food processor and pulse until fine and paste-like. Without a processor, just mix everything by hand.
Spread the meat out, add the salt, MSG, sugar, white pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and cornstarch, pulse to combine, then run the processor until the mixture turns bouncy.
Add 1-2 Tbsp ice water and pulse a few more times until smooth. Transfer to a bowl, cover and refrigerate at least 3 hours, ideally overnight, to firm up.

Chili crisp garlic mayo: cook the garlic cloves in the oil over medium-low until soft and light brown, then turn off the heat and let them coast. Strain out the garlic and cool the oil to about room temperature (no hotter than about 100°F).

In a tall jar, combine the confit garlic, egg yolks, chili crisp with its oil, Dijon, rice vinegar, chilled water and salt. Pour the cooled oil on top, start the stick blender at the bottom and draw it up slowly to emulsify. In a regular blender, stream the oil in instead.
Honey mustard: whisk the yellow mustard, honey and rice vinegar with about 1/3 cup of the chili crisp garlic mayo and a little salt. It thickens as it chills.
Scoop 1 1/2-2 oz portions of the chilled mixture and shape them with damp hands into nuggets no thicker than about 1/2 inch.
Set up three stations: flour, the eggs beaten with a splash of water, and panko pulsed a few times in the processor to make it finer.
Using one dry hand and one wet hand, coat each nugget in flour, then egg, then panko, shaking or draining off the excess each time. Set them on a parchment-lined sheet.
Heat oil in a heavy pot filled about halfway to 350°F. Fry in batches of about six for 3-4 minutes, until golden brown and 165°F inside. Drain.
For Nashville hot, whisk the cayenne, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, light brown sugar, salt and MSG in a heatproof bowl.
Ladle about 1 cup of the hot frying oil into the spices and whisk. Dunk the fried nuggets and coat them thoroughly, rest them on a wire rack for about 30 seconds, then serve with the two sauces.
